answers.question: You said reads may be retried on timeout without limit. Then nothing ends a lookup that keeps getting no answer: listing the customer's orders, re-reading an order after a cancel with no answer, or re-reading a refund. What ends it?
answers.recommended: The agent sends a read with no answer at most twice more, three tries in all. After the third no answer it does what it does when a read fails: for the list, it says it cannot look up the orders right now and changes nothing; for the order re-read, it says it is not known whether the order was cancelled, issues no refund and hands the case to staff; for the refund re-read, it says the refund's status is unknown and hands the case to staff.
answers.reply: > Reads may be retried on timeout without limit; only commit calls are bounded.

answers.question: The cancel call can answer "order not found" for an order the customer's list showed. What does the agent do then?
answers.recommended: It issues no refund, tells the customer the order could not be cancelled, and hands the case to staff with the reason "cancellation unknown".

answers.question: The refund call can answer "order not cancelled". What does the agent do then?
answers.recommended: It does not ask for the refund again, tells the customer the refund was not issued, and hands the case to staff with the reason "refund not issued".
